A question mark is placed on the center of each edge if the causal relation remains to be detected. The question mark will be replaced with the arrows that denote the causal relations between sensors. Each arrow represents a causal link and points from the cause sensor to the effect sensor.

Neighbor sensors are colored blue. Darker blue indicates that the area receives more influences from the neighbor sensors. Bi-directional means that either the stimulus returns after arriving at one sensor or the two sensors receive the same stimulus from another sensor.

Three edge color styles are used based on whether the neighbor sensor belongs to the downstream or upstream. The arrows are colored according to the cause sensor. The lines are colored according to the sensors.
